sections: What DISL 0.4 and FBL 0.4 cannot state yet

items.reason: DISL 10.4 states the properties of a tiered `force` layout and not its constants, and ATD's `algorithm … { force: … }` carries only DISL's settings; the constants stay in the companion's Layout section until a capability or the language states them.

hostCode.behaviour: An entry the binding stores no id for is named by the definition's own scheme: `diagram`, `pinned:<element>` for a locked position, `groups:<element>#<group>` for a group's state.
A lock or a group state whose element is gone is removed on the next write and not reported.
A file the binding cannot read, not YAML or not an activity file, is held as unreadable with the reader's sentence, and nothing is written to it until it reads.
Each edit is planned by the binding as splices of the file; a change to a task or a pull request also sets its updated moment, unless that moment is what was set.
Every edit is one command on the project's history whose undo restores the text the file held.
hostCode.reason: The history and how an exact undo is kept are the host's; the description says each gesture is one command (ATD 12.4).

hostCode.behaviour: The empty canvas offers one Add per toolbox tool and Unlock all positions, unavailable while nothing is locked; the diagram offers Show archived and Hide archived; a group offers Fold and Unfold; an element its derived menu.

Lock position is offered only on an element that is not locked and Unlock position only on one that is; the Open link entries are left out of the menu, a link being opened by its symbol on the canvas.
A rename to nothing is refused with "It needs a name.".
An archived specification is left out unless the archived switch is on, with the relations at either end of it.
Every element is placed by the tiered force layout, rings from the projects outwards, a locked element where it is locked.
A card's size is the definition's, grown by the rows its lists show.
hostCode.reason: How tall a card's shown rows make it is measured by the host's renderer; the notation states the lists and their rows.

hostCode.behaviour: A drop locks each element where it is let go, several at once as one step.
Moving an element under another is refused: "An element of this diagram has no parent to move it under; it is locked where it is dropped.".

A reference to something the file lacks and an id used twice are errors, an entry without an id is information, a file of a newer version is an error, a key the diagram does not read is mentioned once.
The status colours, light and dark, as the definition's theme tokens.
